rulings.challenge_claim: LF: 'The row's confidence label sits above the calibration ceiling that applies to any row spanning a complete chapter.' OL: the row names the opening dated clause a superscription, which blends it with the book's three-header superscription census, and it pairs a whole-verse pointed run of MT 6:5 with a two-word English gloss, the span being coextensive with the chapter while carrying the top confidence band.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENCE: the two lenses meet on the confidence ceiling and that is ONE defect, filed as LF's whole claim and as OL's secondary note; OL's superscription-class and quote-parity items are DISTINCT and also hold. Re-derived: MT ch 6 and WEB ch 6 both carry 13 verses and the span is Isa.6.1-Isa.6.13, so the row is exactly coextensive with the chapter and its 'high' label stands above the medium_low ceiling for whole-chapter spans, with no disclosed exception. DEFECT TWO (OL) is byte-true: the opening clause is בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ (oshb:Isa.6.1, byte tier), a DATE FRAME whose two-token consonantal string stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses), the second being the mid-verse burden-header reference בִּשְׁנַת מ֖וֹת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֑ז (oshb:Isa.14.28, byte tier); the book's superscription census is exactly three vision/ben-Amots headers and 6:1 is not among them, so 'a dated superscription clause' names a class the bytes at that verse do not carry -- though the row's own substrate keys correctly use the vision-report onset rather than a superscription key, so the blend lives in the prose alone and no digit is wrong. DEFECT THREE (OL) is byte-true: device_notes quotes the whole pointed run of MT 6:5 against the two English words “Woe is me!” (web:Isa.6.5), so quote-and-gloss parity is not held. Verified in the row's favour: קָד֧וֹשׁ קָד֛וֹשׁ קָד֖וֹשׁ (oshb:Isa.6.3, byte tier) is rightly held as its own object and not folded into the title census; אֽוֹי (oshb:Isa.6.5, byte tier) is rightly kept apart from the preceding chapter's verse-initial woe lexeme; mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed (PE at MT 6:13 the sole mark inside the span, PE at MT 5:30 at the front seam; tier-3, single-witness); paseq segs sit at MT 6:2 and MT 6:3 (single-witness, count-only) and no ketiv/qere note falls anywhere in MT chs 6-8. NEW FINDING FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: this is a SIXTH whole-chapter span above the cap, and it is NOT on the known-violator roster carried in the peer brief -- that roster is incomplete. Severity raised to medium on that ground: the correction pulls the row into the low-band sidecar and frontier-queue machinery, which is a downstream consequence, not a label tweak.
rulings.remedy: (a) Set confidence to medium_low (the whole-chapter ceiling) or add the explicit disclosed exception the ceiling requires, and carry the row through the low-band sidecar and frontier-queue obligations that the downgrade triggers. (b) In boundary_rationale, replace 'a dated superscription clause' with a date-frame naming, so the header census is not blended; the substrate keys need no change. (c) In device_notes, re-cut the gloss so the pointed run of MT 6:5 is matched by an English quotation of comparable extent, or shorten the pointed run to the clause the gloss actually covers. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: the span-versus-chapter check that killed the original must return a confidence at or below medium_low for a 13-of-13-verse span; the repaired prose must not name any superscription class at this verse, verified against the three-header census; and the quote-and-gloss parity check must pass on the re-cut pair, with every Hebrew run still re-collating at byte tier and a clean normalize dry-run. No boundary change.

rulings.challenge_claim: The one-unit case rests on a single embedded divine frame at MT 7:7 while three further speech onsets inside the same span go unquoted and unweighed, including a resumptive YHWH-speech frame at MT 7:10 whose defective-spelled twin four verses later is treated as a unit-cutting seam.
rulings.grounds: Every element re-derives from bytes. The span carries FOUR verse-initial speech onsets, not one: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶֽל יְשַׁעְיָהוּ֒ (oshb:Isa.7.3, byte tier), כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Isa.7.7, byte tier), וַיּ֣וֹסֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל אָחָ֖ז לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.7.10, byte tier) and וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier) -- all four byte-checked verse-initial -- and only the second is engaged in the row. The plene/defective asymmetry is exact: the MT 7:10 frame's consonantal spelling is a one-verse sweep (sweep: 1 verse) and its defective twin וַיֹּ֣סֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י ע֖וֹד לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.8.5, byte tier) is likewise a one-verse sweep (sweep: 1 verse), and the row treats that second site as a unit-cutting seam while leaving the first silent inside a span. A principled ground for the asymmetry DOES exist -- the MT 7:10 frame sits inside a third-person narrative frame where frame-plus-speech is the default larger unit, while MT 8:5 does not -- but the row never states it in byte terms; it invokes a governance granularity rule BY NAME ('the HYBRID rule that frame plus speech is the default larger unit') in place of the byte argument, which is the register class the challenge also names and which recurs in this writer part. The challenge's residual items verify too: וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב (oshb:Isa.7.3, byte tier) is correctly identified as the remnant NAME site; the Immanu-El count-object is correctly sized (sweep: 3 verses -- MT 7:14, MT 8:8, MT 8:10) with the sign's construal properly held open, which this ruling likewise does not decide; the row's 'name-vs-clause-vs-noun' split names three objects where the attested family runs wider; and the unpointed mention of the bare remnant noun carries no tier label. Mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 7:6 and MT 7:9, PE at MT 7:17 inside the span, PE at MT 6:13 at the front seam; tier-3, single-witness) and no ketiv/qere note falls in this chapter. Severity medium as filed: the frame-plus-speech boundary itself is not displaced, but the internal frame census is incomplete exactly where the row's own reasoning about the neighbouring seam needs it.
rulings.remedy: (a) In boundary_rationale, add the three unengaged verse-initial onsets by splice with tiers named -- וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶֽל יְשַׁעְיָהוּ֒, וַיּ֣וֹסֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל אָחָ֖ז לֵאמֹֽר and וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד -- and state in byte terms why they do not cut here while the defective-spelled resumptive frame at MT 8:5 does: the narrative frame owns the embedded speech in this span and does not in the next. (b) Delete the governance rule name from the rationale and argue the frame ownership from the quoted forms. (c) In device_notes, widen the remnant split to the attested object set and give the bare noun a pointed splice or an explicit skeleton-tier label. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS -- the test that killed the original: a re-census of verse-initial speech onsets across MT 7:1-7:17 must find every onset accounted for in the row's own prose, so a single-frame case cannot stand again; the rewritten rationale must contain no governance-rule name; the asymmetry sentence must cite both spellings with their one-verse sweeps; and every added Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier with a clean normalize dry-run. No respan is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The four-site day-formula recurrence claim is untiered and is not one form in the bytes -- three sites coincide only once accents are stripped and the fourth lacks the leading element entirely -- and that same form is asked to open the row's front seam while being dismissed as non-cutting twice inside it.
rulings.grounds: Every digit and every form re-derives exactly. The three extended openers וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.7.18), וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא (oshb:Isa.7.21) and וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.7.23) each collate at byte tier against their own verses but are pairwise NOT byte-identical -- a byte-tier sweep of the first returns 5 verses and does not reach the other two, while the accent-stripped sweep returns 13 and does (sweep: 5 verses at byte tier, 13 at accent-stripped) -- so the row's untiered 'the formula recurs' covers an accent-stripped-tier identity it never names, against the standing requirement to tier-label every recurrence claim at write time. The fourth asserted site opens בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא (oshb:Isa.7.20, byte tier) WITHOUT the leading element, so one label is covering two distinct attested forms. Only the first of the four is quoted. No digit is supplied: the bare day-formula string stands in 45 verses book-wide (sweep: 45 verses) and the extended form in 13 (sweep: 13 verses), so the device is book-wide rather than peculiar to this unit, and one of the bare sites sits at MT 5:30 outside this chapter. The seam consequence follows on the row's own bytes: the front cut at MT 7:17|7:18 rests on a form that is accent-stripped-identical to the two internal onsets the row expressly declines to cut at, with no byte ground stated for the difference. ONE REFINEMENT FOR THE AUTHOR WAVE, not a softening: the discriminating argument for that same seam exists on the OTHER side of the seam-pair, where the neighbouring row argues a frame-mode shift at MT 7:18; the cure is therefore a SEAM-PAIR cure and must be stated once across both rows. Disclosure objects verify (SAMEKH at MT 7:20, PE at MT 7:25 inside the span, PE at MT 7:17 at the front seam; tier-3, single-witness; one paseq seg at MT 7:18, count-only; no ketiv/qere note in this chapter). Severity medium as filed.
rulings.remedy: (a) In boundary_rationale, tier-label the recurrence: name the accent-stripped-tier identity of the three extended openers and quote at least one further site by splice, and stop counting בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא (oshb:Isa.7.20) with them -- it is a different attested form. (b) Add the digits with their swept objects (bare form 45 verses, extended form 13 verses) so the device is not presented as unit-specific. (c) Argue the front seam from the frame-mode shift at MT 7:18 as the seam-pair partner already does, in ONE formulation shared across the pair, rather than from a form that recurs uncut inside the span. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS -- the test that killed the original: a byte-tier re-collation of the three openers against one another must fail while the accent-stripped one succeeds, and the repaired prose must say so; the seam sentence must name a signal that does NOT recur uncut inside the row's own span; every new Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier with a clean normalize dry-run. No respan is proposed -- the row's bounds are not challenged, only their warrant.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's front-seam driver recurs byte-for-byte inside the row's own four-verse span without cutting there, and the row discloses neither the recurrence nor any ground for the asymmetry; 'a form that occurs twice in four verses and is said to cut only at its first occurrence cannot by itself establish a fresh divine-command frame', so the front seam is carried by a non-discriminating form.
rulings.grounds: The recurrence is byte-true; the inference from it is not, and the refuting bytes are positional. The run וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י stands at MT 8:1 as tokens ONE THROUGH THREE of the verse -- verse-initial -- and the same run recurs byte-identically at MT 8:3 as וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י, but there it sits at tokens SEVEN THROUGH NINE, MID-VERSE, after the first-person narrative clause וָאֶקְרַב֙ אֶל הַנְּבִיאָ֔ה וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן (oshb:Isa.8.3, byte tier). The consonantal string does stand in exactly 2 verses book-wide and both are inside this span (sweep: 2 verses), exactly as challenged -- but the two occurrences are not positionally equivalent candidate cut sites: one is a verse-initial frame onset, the other an embedded speech tag inside a running narrative sentence, and verse-initial position is the onset criterion this book's frame spine applies throughout (the woe census is role-split by it; the oracle headers are counted as verse-initial). The challenge compares an onset with a speech tag without naming that difference, so its central inference does not carry: the row's driver IS discriminating on its own bytes. The row's argument does not in any case rest on the form's uniqueness -- it argues the front seam by contrast with the preceding cycle's impersonal repeated-formula pattern, and the rear seam from the materially different resumptive frame וַיֹּ֣סֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י ע֖וֹד לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.8.5, byte tier), a one-verse sweep, which the challenge itself concedes is well founded. Nothing else in the row is defective: the unit_type matches the operative sign-act class for this span, the span is four verses so no whole-chapter ceiling applies, mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 8:4 the sole mark inside the span, PE at MT 7:25 at the front seam; tier-3, single-witness), a paseq seg sits at MT 8:4 (single-witness, count-only), and no ketiv/qere note falls in MT chs 6-8. The row would read more strongly if it named the positional discriminator outright, but its stated warrant does not depend on it, so no work order issues.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row decides a construal it simultaneously declares held -- reading the closing formation of MT 8:8 as a vocative address and resting its rear-seam sentence on that reading -- and it attaches a byte-tier label to an unpointed run that collates at skeleton.
rulings.grounds: THE TIER DEFECT IS UPHELD AND IS THE SERIOUS ONE: device_notes attaches an explicit byte-tier label to the UNPOINTED two-token mention of the formation, and an unpointed run reaches skeleton tier, not byte, against its own cited verse -- a mention-grade form carrying a quotation-grade label, in a campaign where only byte tier is quotation-grade. The pointed run itself is sound: עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל (oshb:Isa.8.8, byte tier). THE PARITY DEFECT IS UPHELD: boundary_rationale quotes an eleven-token pointed run of MT 8:8 against the two English words “O Immanuel” (web:Isa.8.8). THE 'DECIDES A HELD CONSTRUAL' CHARGE IS REFRAMED, NOT ADOPTED AS FILED: the rear seam does NOT rest on the vocative reading. Its stated ground is the addressee shift at the following verse, and that shift is byte-explicit and independent -- MT 8:9 opens with a plural imperative and a named addressee -- so the seam stands whether or not the formation at MT 8:8 is an address. What IS defective is narrower and real: the row writes 'HELD' and then 'is read here as a vocative address' in the same note, asserting a form-class label that the staged extract cannot verify (no morphology layer is staged, and the suffixed form אַרְצְךָ֖ carries no vocative particle), while the standing rule makes form-class labels byte-checkable claims held to the discipline of digits. THIS RULING DOES NOT DECIDE THE CONSTRUAL: the address-versus-clause relation across MT 7:14, MT 8:8 and MT 8:10 is a held classic and is left exactly where the row left it. Verified in the row's favour: the front seam is byte-sound -- וַיֹּ֣סֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י ע֖וֹד לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.8.5, byte tier) is a distinct resumptive frame, a one-verse sweep, not the command frame of the preceding unit -- and mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 8:8 inside the span, SAMEKH at MT 8:4 at the front seam; tier-3, single-witness), with no ketiv/qere note in this chapter. Severity stays medium: tier mislabelling is the class the campaign treats as quotation-grade risk, even though no boundary moves.
rulings.remedy: (a) In device_notes, either replace the unpointed mention with the pointed splice עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל from oshb:Isa.8.8 and keep the byte-tier label, or keep the unpointed mention and relabel it skeleton tier -- one or the other, not the present pairing. (b) Re-cut the quote-and-gloss pair in boundary_rationale so the pointed run and the English quotation cover comparable extents. (c) Rewrite the held sentence so the form-class is HELD rather than read: state that the formation closes the unit and that its address-versus-clause construal is disclosed and not decided, with no morphology layer staged to settle it. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS -- the test that killed the original: every Hebrew run must re-collate at the tier its own label claims, so an unpointed run may no longer carry a byte-tier label; the parity check must pass on the re-cut pair; and the rewritten note must contain no asserted form-class label. The rear seam needs no change and no respan is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: 'The row's rear boundary at web:Isa.8.18 severs an undisclosed lexical inclusio that runs through web:Isa.8.20.' OL: the rear seam cuts through a two-noun pairing the bytes attest in only two verses in the whole book with no cross-seam cohesion disclosed; inside the span two distinct objects on one consonantal string go unnamed; and the front-seam run opens on a subordinating particle binding back across the seam.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENCE: both lenses land on the SAME defect at the rear seam -- an undisclosed byte-attested pairing straddling it -- and OL adds two DISTINCT further defects. The shared finding re-derives exactly: the row's own closing quote is צ֖וֹר תְּעוּדָ֑ה חֲת֥וֹם תּוֹרָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.8.16, byte tier) and the next unit opens לְתוֹרָ֖ה וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.8.20, byte tier), the same two nouns in reverse order; one of the pair stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide and both are these (sweep: 2 verses -- MT 8:16 and MT 8:20), so the PAIRING is unique to the two verses, it straddles this row's own rear seam at MT 8:18|8:19, both witnesses render it, and the row's device note discloses only an internal uncertainty about where quoted divine speech yields to the prophet's voice. A byte-attested device straddling a row's own seam argues continuity against that seam unless disclosed, so the non-disclosure is a real defect. REFINEMENT ON A SHARED DIGIT: the companion count of 5 verses is a SPELLING-scoped sweep of the absolute form (MT 2:3, 8:16, 8:20, 42:21, 51:4) presented in both packets as a count of the noun itself; the construct and suffixed spellings are outside it, so the object must be named as a spelling -- the finding does not depend on that digit, resting entirely on the two-verse exclusivity of the other noun. OL's second item holds: the row refers to the sanctuary-and-stumbling-stone judgment in English only while the span's bytes carry וּלְצ֨וּר מִכְשׁ֜וֹל (oshb:Isa.8.14, byte tier) two verses before the differently-pointed token opening MT 8:16 -- two distinct objects on one contiguous consonantal string (sweep: 23 verses carry that string book-wide), neither named. OL's third item holds and is minor: the front-seam run is quoted honestly and its ownership is correctly divine, but it opens כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה (oshb:Isa.8.11, byte tier), a subordinating particle binding back across the seam the row asks it to open, unnoted. Disclosure objects verify (SAMEKH at MT 8:15 and MT 8:18 inside the span, SAMEKH at MT 8:10 at the front seam; tier-3, single-witness; no ketiv/qere note in this chapter). Severity medium as both lenses filed it.
rulings.remedy: DISCLOSURE WORK ONLY -- the respan is NOT author work. (a) In device_notes, disclose the cross-seam pairing: splice צ֖וֹר תְּעוּדָ֑ה חֲת֥וֹם תּוֹרָ֖ה and לְתוֹרָ֖ה וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה with tiers named, state the two-verse exclusivity of the rarer noun with its swept object, and say plainly that the pairing straddles this row's rear seam. This is a SEAM-PAIR disclosure shared with the following row and must ship as ONE formulation. (b) In device_notes, name the two objects on the shared consonantal string by splice -- וּלְצ֨וּר מִכְשׁ֜וֹל against the differently-pointed token opening MT 8:16 -- rather than in English. (c) In boundary_rationale, note that the front-seam run opens on a subordinating particle and say why it is still read as an onset. BOUNDARY PROPOSAL, FOR BOSS ADOPTION ONLY: the bracket argues the unit may run through MT 8:20; that respan is a proposal requiring explicit boss adoption and must NOT be executed by the author wave. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS -- the test that killed the original: a cross-seam device sweep over the row's own rear seam must return the pairing and find it disclosed in the row's prose; the rarer noun's digit must name its swept object; every added Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier with a clean normalize dry-run.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the front boundary 'rests on a bare topic-shift rationale that is not a recognized tier-1 frame marker, and it opens inside an undisclosed lexical bracket spanning web:Isa.8.16-web:Isa.8.20.' OL: neither seam is argued from the bytes -- the front cut ignores the pairing its own second verse inherits across that seam, and the rear cut is justified by the row's administrative range rather than by the text, with the one cross-seam signal it does disclose reduced to tone.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENCE at the front seam, and the two framings are NOT the same defect: LF says no tier-1 marker exists there, OL says an attested cohesion signal was ignored. THE REAR-SEAM ITEM (OL only) IS THE STRONGEST AND IS UPHELD: the row's rear boundary is justified in its own prose as 'the last verse of this part's assigned range' -- range administration, not evidence, and range-administration language inside row prose, which the register rules bar outright. THE FRONT-SEAM COHESION ITEM IS UPHELD: the unit's second verse opens לְתוֹרָ֖ה וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.8.20, byte tier), the reversed twin of צ֖וֹר תְּעוּדָ֑ה חֲת֥וֹם תּוֹרָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.8.16, byte tier) three verses back across the front seam, with the rarer noun standing in exactly 2 verses book-wide, both of them here (sweep: 2 verses) -- a byte-level fact bearing directly on this seam that the row never mentions, its front-seam argument being purely topical. LF'S 'NOT A RECOGNIZED TIER-1 MARKER' IS OVERSTATED AND IS THE REFINEMENT: the front verse opens וְכִֽי יֹאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵיכֶ֗ם (oshb:Isa.8.19, byte tier), whose second-person plural addressee element IS explicit in the bytes and does mark a shift from the first-person prophetic testimony closing MT 8:18 -- addressee shifts are tier-1 where explicit, so a tier-1-eligible element is present at the cut. The defect is therefore that the row leaves that available byte ground unstated and rests on a topic label, not that no marker exists; a cure that merely adds the topic label to the evidence would not pass. VERIFIED IN THE ROW'S FAVOUR: the zone-A rear-edge dual-cite is written correctly (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1) and lands on the right content, the Zebulun/Naphtali line; the held handling of the MT 8:22 / oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1 sound pair is right -- מְע֣וּף צוּקָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.8.22, byte tier) against כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier) are NOT a contiguous consonantal match, so no sweep digit supports them and no verbatim label may be attached, and the staged extract carries no morphology layer to confirm a shared root; and parashah disclosure is right, no mark falling inside MT 8:19-8:22 (0 marks over those 4 verses) with the SAMEKH at MT 8:18 named at the front seam (tier-3, single-witness, its in-span absence carrying no weight either way). No ketiv/qere note falls in this chapter or at the zone edge. Severity medium as both lenses filed it.
rulings.remedy: (a) In boundary_rationale, replace the bare topic-shift ground with the byte ground actually present: splice וְכִֽי יֹאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵיכֶ֗ם from oshb:Isa.8.19 with its tier named and argue the front seam from the explicit second-person plural addressee against the first-person testimony closing MT 8:18. (b) Delete the range-administration clause from boundary_rationale and argue the rear seam from the text -- the disclosed zone-edge continuity may be characterised, with its dual kept, but the row must state a textual ground or lower its confidence accordingly. (c) Carry the seam-pair cross-seam disclosure of the two-noun pairing named in the preceding row's remedy -- ONE formulation across both rows, tiers and swept object named. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS -- the tests that killed the original: the register sweep must find no range-administration or file-order language anywhere in row prose; the rear-seam sentence must name a form quoted from a cited verse's own bytes rather than an assigned range; the front-seam sentence must cite the addressee element rather than a topic label; the cross-seam device sweep must find the pairing disclosed; every Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier with a clean normalize dry-run and every zone-A ref keeps its dual. BOUNDARY PROPOSAL, FOR BOSS ADOPTION ONLY: any respan following from the bracket is a proposal, never author work.
